notes: Researcher notes (written before verification; where they differ, the clusters field and the verification field prevail). Clusters: FE = fasteners.eu + boltport (one lineage by the strict convention of earlier verifications), westfieldfasteners, fasten.it, CN = globalfastener (ISO 7380-1:2011, DIN EN ISO 7380(-1):2011, ISO 7380-1:2022, ISO 7380:2004 pages) + fullerfasteners, DE = theo-schrauben + schrauben-lexikon (one dataset), fastenright (k, t, s, pitch only), boltsfastener (M3-M12: k, t, s), woodstockindustrial and fastenerdata (pitch / key size only: their head columns carry no max wording). Tier B (amesweb calculator, ISO 7380-1:2011) carries the same values for every kept cell but is not counted. dw_min is deliberately not carried: fasteners.eu, westfield and globalfastener's 2011 page agree on 5 / 6.84 / 8.74 / 9.57 / 13.07 / 16.57 / 19.68 / 26.68 (2011 edition), but the only 2022-edition page found (globalfastener) prints 4.97 / 6.66 / 8.41 / 9.26 / 12.48 / 15.7 / 18.84 / 25.28, i.e. the value changed with the edition and the current-edition value has one source. rf_max (3.7 / 4.6 / 5.75 / 6.15 / 7.95 / 9.8 / 11.2 / 15.3) has only two counted clusters (westfield 'dome radius rf max', globalfastener 'r3 max' defined by its drawing); fasteners.eu prints the same numbers in a row called 'r1' that its own drawing does not define (drawing says rf), and the amesweb calculator prints them as rf,max - neither is counted. lMaxStd_2011: no page gives a per-size longest standard length with a header that says so. NOT used: itafasteners button-head page (its table is the flanged ISO 7380-2 one), engineersedge iso_socket_button_head (plain head columns, 'Flat Width' 2.045), wuerth and accu (bot challenge), westfield / tdm-neva PDFs. fastenright lists dk 7.5 (M4), 18 (M10) and k 6 (M12): older / different range, so its k vote is missing for M12. westfield's 't min.' row repeats its 'w min.' row from M4 up (page glitch). For the verifier: the globalfastener ISO 7380-1 pages carry two or three short table footnotes (e min = 1.14 s min, the 80 % load note) next to the table - judged to be a dimension table, not a reproduction of the standard's text; b_ref and every other kept column rest on exactly three clusters at minimum (b: fasteners.eu, westfield, globalfastener+Fuller). Verifier (2026-11-11, fresh downloads, own parser): column b_ref_2011 removed - the 2022 edition changed b for M16 to 3d (foreword of ISO 7380-1:2022, official preview), so the statement above that only dw_min differs between the editions is wrong, and globalfastener's 2022-labelled page (b = 44 for M16) is stale on that row. fastenright and boltsfastener are not counted. t_min stands on exactly 3 clusters (fasteners.eu+Boltport, fasten.it, globalfastener+Fuller).

verification.checks_done: Verifier (different from the researcher) re-downloaded on 2026-11-11 with curl + browser User-Agent every listed page, all HTTP 200: fasteners.eu ISO/7380, boltport iso-7380, westfieldfasteners ScrewBolt-SHBtn-M, fasten.it din_en_iso_7380-1, fullerfasteners iso-7380-1, globalfastener detail_3005 + the 2022, DIN EN 2011 and 2004 pages, theo-schrauben, schrauben-lexikon, fastenright sk07, boltsfastener, woodstockindustrial, fastenerdata (amesweb fetched only to confirm it is HTML; not counted). Tables re-read with the verifier's own parser (researcher's raw files and scripts not used); drawings on the fasteners.eu, fasten.it and globalfastener pages opened. For the edition question the official preview page of ISO 7380-1:2022 (standards.iteh.ai, foreword) was read; iso.org answered with a bot challenge. Candidate 8 rows x 6 columns: b_ref_2011 removed (edition-dependent). Remaining 8 rows x 5 columns = 40 cells: pitch, dk and k are stated exactly by 5 clusters, s by 7, t_min by 3 (fasteners.eu + Boltport / fasten.it / globalfastener + Fuller; westfield agrees only at M3). Physical checks recomputed: dk / d between 1.75 and 1.90, k = 0.55 d, t_min = 0.52 s, s < dk, every column strictly increasing. No PDF, document-sharing page, login page or page of standard text among the counted sources (globalfastener carries three short table footnotes, fasten.it one scope sentence: judged dimension-table pages).
problems: Column b_ref_2011 removed: not edition-independent as the record claimed. The foreword of ISO 7380-1:2022 (official preview) states that b was increased to 3d for partially threaded M16 screws (48, not 44). The three clusters behind 18 ... 44 are 2011-content pages; globalfastener's 2022-labelled page still prints 44 and is the only 2022-labelled page with a b row; fasteners.eu and westfield do not state an edition. If fasteners.eu and westfield were merged (identical row set and order, the standard's own), b would have 2 clusters in any case. Option for the caller instead of removing the column: keep b for M3 - M12 and remove the M16 row (7 rows x 6 columns).

The five kept columns are edition-independent on the evidence available: 2011-labelled pages (fasten.it, globalfastener x2) and 2022-labelled pages (Boltport, globalfastener) agree cell by cell, and the 2022 foreword lists no change to P, dk max, k max, s or t min (it lists b for M16, dw min = 0.92 dk min, e min rounded to 2 decimals, t max added, w -> wb, rf definition, lengths, tensile loads, marking). standard = ISO 7380-1 without an edition is therefore honest for what is left; standard_full rewritten.

t_min has zero margin: exactly fasteners.eu + Boltport / fasten.it / globalfastener + Fuller in rows M4 - M16. Westfield's t min row prints 0.30 / 0.38 / 0.74 / 1.05 / 1.45 / 1.63 / 2.25 from M4 up (its w min row repeated) and agrees only at M3. fastenright and boltsfastener print the same t min values under a t min. header but their tables follow another head-diameter range (M4 7.5, M10 18; fastenright M12 k 6) and are not counted; fastenerdata has a t column without min wording.

fasten.it is counted here although its ASME B18.3 pages were rejected for the inch families: this page states the unit correctly (mm), its max / min columns are consistent with every other source, and no cell deviates. It is the third cluster for t_min, so that column depends on it.

Independence of fasteners.eu, westfield and globalfastener: all three list the 21 rows of the standard's table in the same order with e min to 3 decimals, which follows from the standard itself; they differ in symbols (fasteners.eu r1 / dL, westfield rf / dL with plain-language names and an extra M2.5 column, globalfastener r3 / d1 / r1 / r2) and in errors (only westfield has the t min glitch) - counted as separate transcriptions. Boltport stays in the fasteners.eu cluster by the strict convention although its 2022 page has a different layout.
Catalogue mismatch for the caller: the catalogue row carries rf_max, dw_min (2022 values), b_ref_2011 and lMaxStd_2011, none of which is in the verified record.

Not checked: the standard's tables (only the public preview foreword was read; iso.org blocked by a bot challenge). rf_max, dw_min and lMaxStd_2011 stay dropped as in the researcher's record (recount of rf_max: westfield and globalfastener only; fasteners.eu prints the numbers under r1).
